stories.summary: The boss of Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition has responded to reports that staff at the studio are worried they will lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, and promised the next Gears game won’t take as long to make.

sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day Studio Boss Insists 'The Next Game Will Not Take Nearly as Long' to Make, Responds to Layoff Concern
sources.text: The boss of Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition has responded to reports that staff at the studio are worried they will lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, and promised the next Gears game won’t take as long to make. Earlier this month, Eurogamer reported on serious internal concern that layoffs would hit The Coalition after the release of E-Day. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case,' which is very unusual," one source told the site. "We're just expecting the next wave [of layoffs], or being reorganized under Activision or something later this year," claimed another. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business has seen nearly 2,000 people cut already this financial year, with more to come. A number of studios have left the business or are in the process of closing down. Microsoft has also reorganized its studios, bringing Halo and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under Call of Duty developer Activision, and Grounded developer Obsidian under Fallout developer Bethesda. The Coalition has, for the most part, avoided the cuts, although E-Day's story director was laid off just one week before the game's early access launch . The BBC put Eurogamer’s report to The Coalition studio head Mike Crump, who danced around the issue in his response. "What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we need to focus on the things that we can control,” Crump said. "For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that." No guarantee, then, that The Coalition will escape the fate suffered by so many at Xbox this summer. But Crump did suggest there are plans for more Gears of War games. He called E-Day a "great foundation" for future games in the series, and said "the next game will not take nearly as long" to make. As for what the next Gears game is, in June 2024, Microsoft pledged to continue the story of Gears of War and wrap up the cliffhanger posed by Gears 5's ending, despite creating a prequel first with E-Day. The question is, will The Coalition get the chance to make it? Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. sources.title: Gears Of War Boss Dodges Question About Future Layoffs, Promises Next Game Will Come Sooner
sources.text: Xbox is currently in the middle of its big corporate “reset, ” which has involved the company shuffling around franchises and teams while it continues to lay off workers . And while this has all been happening, The Coalition launched Gears of War: E-Day , a well-received Xbox-exclusive prequel to the original trilogy. Many are wondering what the studio’s future holds. Coalition studio head Mike Crump says the team is focused on what it “can control.” In a new interview with the BBC, Crump was directly asked about the recent Eurogamer report that claimed numerous Coalition devs remained nervous about the Xbox laying off staff after shipping E-Day . The studio boss didn’t share any details about the studio’s immediate future or if cuts were coming, and instead suggested the goal is just to make good games people like. He even promised that the next Gears game won’t take seven years to arrive like this one did. “What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we just need to focus on the things that we can control,” said Crump. “For us that’s about shipping a great game that people are going to love, and I feel like, as a team, we’ve done that.” According to Crump, E-Day is a “great foundation” for future Gears titles, and he told the BBC that “the next game will not take nearly as long” to create. He then added something that sounds almost like Crump is trying to convince any Xbox leadership listening to not to make cuts to the studio , as it would disrupt the decades of experience the team has built up since it took over Gears of War back in 2014. “We’ve got a great team here. And the leadership team in particular has worked together for upwards of 20 years,” said Crump. “So there’s definitely a continuity of knowledge and experience.” The Coalition has mostly dodged Xbox’s layoffs , though the game’s story director and others were laid off last month , as Kotaku reported. sources.title: Gears of War boss says the next game won't take seven years to make as he dances around the question of layoffs
sources.text: The Coalition, the Microsoft-owned studio behind Gears of War: E-Day, Gears 4 and Gears 5 has mostly survived the wide-ranging cuts and layoffs initiated by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma in her attempt to bring the gaming division back to profitability . But as Eurogamer reported, now that Gears of War: E-Day has shipped, many within The Coalition fear they're going to be laid off shortly afterwards , potentially missing out on bonuses. Now, in an interview with the BBC , studio head Mike Crump was asked about the report and whether cuts are planned for the Canadian studio. Crump didn't offer specifics about the future of the studio, however. "What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we just we need to focus on the things that we can control," said Crump. "For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that." E-Day has been fairly well-received by critics and embraced by players, boasting the series' best numbers on Steam . In the Eurogamer E-Day campaign review , Dom Peppiatt said the game proves there's still life left in the aging franchise. But the big question is whether that is going to be enough to keep The Coalition safe and convince Xbox to invest in a future project. E-Day is an Xbox console exclusive - a decision reportedly hastily made just before the game's big summer reveal - which limits its audience and sales potential. "Gears has been an exclusive franchise to Xbox for 20 years now. It's sort of entwined deeply with the brand," said Crump. Asked how the studio measures success, the studio head said that while numbers are important, there's more that gets taken into account. Said Crump, "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? "Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware." After shipping Gears 5 in 2019, it took The Coalition seven years to develop and release Gears of War: E-Day. To that end, the studio boss believes E-Day makes for a "great foundation" for future sequels, and promises the next game "will not take nearly as long" to develop. The Coalition has not announced any future projects.

sources.title: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor begins bringing furloughed staff back
sources.text: One source says more than half of the pre-furlough team is now back on the payroll Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has started bringing back staff it furloughed ahead of the game's launch. In a statement shared on Bluesky , CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio "started the process of returning more of our team back to work" this week, but stopped short of confirming how many people are returning. Foertsch said asking staff to step away was "an incredibly difficult decision" that followed "unexpected business developments outside of our control," but was necessary to "eventually bring as many people back as possible." A person familiar with the situation told Game File that more than half of the pre-furlough team is now back on the payroll, with others still unpaid. Game File has reported that furloughed staff keep their employee status but receive neither salary nor benefits. Bit Reactor furloughed "many of its workers" in the weeks before the game's release, a decision it said was made "before it was clear how the launch would go." Sources told Game File at the time that 80% of staff were furloughed, leaving a skeleton crew to address post-launch bugs.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Bit Reactor CEO Welcomes Return of Some Furloughed Staff for 'Continued Support' of Star Wars Zero Company
sources.text: Bit Reactor, the developer of Star Wars Zero Company, has begun returning some of its staff to the team after furloughing an estimated 80% of employees just before the game’s launch. Bit Reactor’s CEO Greg Foertsch revealed the news in a public post on October 7, where he explained that the furloughs were necessary to “help us eventually bring as many people back as possible.” Foertsh said that bringing these staff members back to Bit Reactor was an “important step forward” in the studio’s “continued support for Zero Company,” and that the team looks forward to sharing more updates about the game “soon.” “Having to ask team members to step away after we navigated unexpected business developments outside of our control and so close to launch was an incredibly difficult decision,” Foertsh wrote. “...This team means a tremendous amount to me, and I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together. Thank you to our fans for the incredible response to the game and for supporting us along this journey.” Sources with information about the situation told GameFile that the number of Bit Reactor’s payrolled staff now account for “more than half of what it had been ahead of the furloughs,” meaning that there is still a sizeable chunk of furloughed staff who aren’t getting paid. Star Wars Zero Company launched in August 2026 to rave reviews, getting a sparkling nine out of 10 from our reviewers here at IGN who praised it for being an “excellent tactical game that does a fantastic job of slathering on the same cinematic look and feel we saw in Respawn's Star Wars Jedi games, incorporating strong characters and a storyline that's refreshingly centered on non-Force users and a non-traditional villain.” Despite its success, much of Bit Reactor’s staff were placed on leave without pay just before Zero Company launched, with reports indicating around 80% of employees were affected. This has become a recurring trend within the game development industry, to the point where Gears of War: E-Day developers were overcome with worry that they would get laid off after “crunching hard” to get the game out on time. This is the latest news to get revealed about Zero Company after GameFile uncovered legal documents revealing that the game was initially pitched as a title within the Titanfall universe , with specific connections to Apex Legends . While this pitch ultimately didn’t go through, it’s certainly intriguing enough to make us wonder what such a game would have looked like, had it actually been made. sources.text: "We look forward to sharing more updates regarding Bit Reactor and Zero Company" Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor is actively "returning more of our team back to work" after furloughing staff right before launch due to apparent budget issues. In a post on Bluesky , Bit Reactor CEO Greg Foertsch confirms the great de-furloughing began this week, which it calls "an important step in our continued support for Zero Company." The statement confirms much of what was reported around the launch. "Having to ask team members to step away after we navigated unexpected business developments out of our control and so close to launch was an incredibly difficult decision, but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible," Foertsch continues. It's unclear how many, if any, developers may be laid off at the end of this return process. Whereas layoffs result in immediate job cuts, a furlough is essentially a period of unpaid absence or reduced hours which is generally enacted to lower costs and overhead during a period of some kind of financial hardship. Game File's Stephen Totilo reports "over half" of the team has now returned. "This team means a tremendous amount to me, and I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together," Foertsch adds. "Thank you to our fans for the incredible response to the game and for supporting us along this journey. We look forward to sharing more updates regarding Bit Reactor and Zero Company soon." Star Wars Zero Company saw some of the strongest reviews of any Star Wars game in recent years. We called it a solid strategy RPG after getting our feet wet, and it's sitting comfortably at a score of 84 on Metacritic. On Steam, Zero Company has "very positive" reviews. It was an utter shame to see the team behind it struggling even after shipping a great game, and it's good to see them getting back on their feet. sources.title: STAR WARS: Galactic Racer — Crashing with Consequence in Runs-Based Racing
sources.text: Allow us to set the scene. Three corners from the finish line, another racer shunts your repulsorcraft into an adjacent boulder, sending you careening into the toxic wastes of Sentinel I. You try to correct your course. Too late. The vehicle that took you 4 tours and 23 races to tune is now scattered across the track, your League Token is forfeit, and the tour is over. These are the moments that are instrumental in your journey to become Champion of the Galactic League, and the moments that the team built around STAR WARS: Galactic Racer — available today for XBOX Series X|S. “We’ve got a history of trying to make failure fun,” says Creative Director at Fuse Games Kieran Crimmins. “Failure can be this big, spectacular, exciting, interesting and rewarding experience in the game. Our wreck-out system is meant to be the ethos of how Fuse approach game making. Crashing isn’t just a big spectacle; it has consequence as well as mechanical rewards so you can learn something for your next run.” “Failure is fuel, which is where our runs-based mechanic comes into play,” adds Co-founder and Head of Content at Fuse Games Steve Uphill. “It’s the opportunity to try again, and when you get the right combination of builds, parts and upgrades, failure makes winning feel hard earned, but so much more rewarding and creates a powerful and unique player story.” In STAR WARS: Galactic Racer , player persistence is the key to success. Kieran explains what runs-based actually means, and how Fuse Games adds their own spin on the widely used term: “For us, runs-based is a replayable loop that allows you to experiment with a new way to play every time, see how far you get with it, and if you fail, you still get some great rewards to go again so you can try with a new combination of parts and abilities.” “From start to end, the process looks like this: the player starts by choosing which vehicle you want to attempt that run in, whether it be a skim speeder, speeder bike, or landspeeder. They all have slightly different playstyles and attributes. Then, you pick a Racer Style, which gives your build a baseline direction. So, if you wanted to make an afterburner build or a cooled build for example, you start with that Racer Style, then select which abilities, parts and upgrades complement it at the end of each race. Depending how well you do in the races, you’ll also get financial rewards that you can spend at the shop in between planets. There’s always going to be the temptation to try out new abilities or upgrades, but these are rewarded randomly, so there’s an element of luck involved. Most will be able to synergise with your build in some way, so it’s up to your knowledge and creativity for that limited set to find a path to success. If you’re lucky, you’ll win the league. If you don’t win the league, however, the path to success is filled with challenges, rivals, and events to test you. Crash too many times and you’ll ‘wreck out’, or you fail a high-stakes event, then you’ll lose a League Token and be back to the start.” Failure is an important part of the game’s mechanics, which is why ‘wrecking out’ is so instrumental to gameplay: “You have a certain number of crashes that you’re allowed to do in any race,” says Kieran, “not all events have it, but a lot of them do. If you use all your crashes, then you’ll ‘wreck out’ and have to start from the beginning of that tour. Crucially, we wanted there to be an element of consequence in the gameplay. Your decisions matter across every part of the game, so you need some sort of finite failure state for your decisions to matter, and wrecking out felt like a great manifestation of that. Every corner matters, every interaction with another racer matters. It forces you to think about what choices you make and what you’re doing, rather than driving with abandon.” It’s this element of player agency and choice that makes the runs-based loop in STAR WARS: Galactic Racer so satisfying. Kieran expresses the importance of player choice: “If you think about playing in its most base form, it isn’t someone tells you what to do then you do it. That’s a job, that’s instruction. Instead, we provide a play space full of fun things. Play is the choice to arrange them in the way that you want, and creating your own moments and journeys. The power of a good player story is the absolute power of play in general.” And that agency doesn’t end when the run does. Kieran continues: “There are two important progression routes for a run. The first is your stat build-up, where you get temporary stats for each vehicle like cornering, resilience, ramjet, afterburner etc. This allows you to dial into your playstyle as well as your build, and you can add points to make those base stats different. The second one is your combination of parts. As standard, you’ll get to install up to five parts. Each of those parts have different rarity, and you build those up as you go through the different events, either from the shop or as event awards. They all do vastly different things and synergise in different ways, some even develop faults that change builds even further. The combinations in the parts system is so vast, I’m not even sure we’ve seen every single combination yet!” “You also get permanent progression outside of each tour that you can put into one of your vehicle types. So, it’s the same set of stats, but they’ll stay there for the rest of your enjoyment of the game. Once you beat a tour, you open up a larger pool of parts. You’ll also unlock new ‘favors’ that you can equip to further modify the rules for the next run. Another form of permanent progression is the ability to upgrade your Racer Styles, so you can unlock all sorts of different ways to play.” These features carry over to multiplayer, too: “In multiplayer, we wanted to create a runs-based system that worked. sources.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Multiplayer Party Limit Will Be Doubled Via Update
sources.text: Star Wars: Galactic Racer has broadly proven to be a smash hit with critics, and fans seem similarly enthusiastic, but developer Fuse Games has heard the concern regarding multiplayer party sizes and has responded via the game’s official social media. Resultingly, it appears we should be able to expect an update to increase the multiplayer party size from three to six players at some point within the next few weeks. “Thank you so much for your feedback and we’d like to let you and everyone on this thread know that we hear you,” the developer responded to various fans raising the concern online. “We’re working on an update to increase the party size from three to six players, with the aim of releasing it within the first few weeks of launch.” More details will be available soon, the developer noted. IGN’s Star Wars: Galactic Racer review called it “a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer… that has successfully lit the afterburners on a long-dormant slice of the Star Wars universe.” Luke Reilly is an award-winning journalist with 23 years of media experience across Official PlayStation Magazine, Australian 360, and IGN – which he joined in 2011. sources.text: The game currently supports parties of 3 players Star Wars: Galactic Racer developer Fuse Games has announced that the game’s multiplayer party limit will be doubled in an upcoming update. At the time of writing, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ‘s multiplayer parties are currently limited to three players, a limitation that was met with dissapointment from players who wanted to play with more of their friends. Now, in a social media post, the Star Wars: Galactic Racer account has confirmed that this restriction will be eased in a future update. Responding to a fan on X , the account wrote, “Thank you so much for your feedback and we’d like to let you and everyone on this thread know that we hear you! We’re working on an update to increase the party size from 3 to 6 players, with the aim of releasing it within the first few weeks of launch. More details coming soon!” Thank you so much for your feedback and we'd like to let you and everyone on this thread know that we hear you! We're working on an update to increase the party size from 3 to 6 players, with the aim of releasing it within the first few weeks of launch. More details coming soon! While no specific date for this update was shared, it should comes as good news to fans. Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been met with critical acclaim and strong player support, but issues like the lack of private multiplayer races, and this small party restriction remain. VGC’s review of the game called it a “modern racing classic” that “absolutely nails what it is trying to do”. “It is a high-octane racer that’s endless fun to play, and it looks fantastic,” we said. “This would have been a great game with a standard single-player mode, but what is here is inventive and engaging. I’d have loved a few silly classic characters and another planet or two, but this is a game I’ll return to for a long time.” Star Wars: Galactic Racer was released earlier this week. At the time of writing, players with Amazon Prime can play the single-player portion of the game via Amazon’s Luna service at no extra cost. “We’ve always believed Luna players deserve to be in the action from day one, and Star Wars: Galactic Racer makes that a reality for the first time,” Amazon head of gaming Jeff Gattis told GamesIndustry.biz in a statement.

sources.text: Forza Horizon 6 's highly-anticipated release on PlayStation 5 has apparently been delayed to 2027, according to new information. Yes, this is not the first time we've heard that - The Verge's Tom Warren and IGN said as much in late August . Forza Horizon 6 studio Playground Games countered those claims days later, however, saying the open-world driving game has not been pushed back , while opening wishlisting for it on the PlayStation Store. Now, Dealabs' reliable leaker billbil-kun has added their voice to the noise, going further by revealing a specific, 26th January release date. They also speculated that an official announcement is coming this week alongside the opening of pre-orders. "We've done our own investigation, and our research has paid off. Yes, we've managed to obtain the exact release date of Forza Horizon 6 on PS5," wrote French insider billbil-kun (via machine translation). According to billbil-kun, the game is priced £59.99 in the UK and €69.99 in the rest of Europe. A physical version - with a disc - will also be available at retail. Incidentally, billbil-kun wasn't able to verify whether a Premium Edition is being offered on PS5. On PC and Xbox, the Premium Edition includes an expansion pass, car pass and various other in-game bonuses. If purchased ahead of launch, the Premium Edition also grants up to four days of early access. It's possible Xbox is planning to release a digital-only Premium Edition on PS5, which wouldn't be visible to billbil-kun's typically retail-based sources. Just yesterday, Playground Games issued a statement on X apologising for a general lack of communication about Forza Horizon 6 and assuring players it was listening to feedback. The developer also promised to look into changing the way it communicates with players going forward. Of course, it's always possible the decision to delay Horizon 6 to January was made after Playground announced it was on track for a 2026 release, even though it's been almost exactly one month since. sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day studio finds a way to get more performance from Xbox Series S - one that other Xbox games could probably use
sources.text: As a first-party Xbox title, Gears of War: E-Day is under pressure to look good and run well on Xbox consoles. This is especially challenging to do on Series S, due to the console's limited computing power compared to Series X. But developer The Coalition has discovered a clever way of circumventing the Series S' limited memory pool. Gears of War: E-Day has densely-detailed environments that require a lot of system memory (RAM), which is a struggle for Xbox Series S' 10GB of GDDR6 RAM. The Coalition's solution was to offload some of that data onto the console's ultra-fast NVMe SSD storage drive. Digital Foundry reported on the tech behind it, which was co-developed by Xbox's Advanced Technology Group. For some context, NVMe SSD drives are made up of RAM modules of their own, so they can act as additional RAM when needed. As fast as they are, however, NVMe drives aren't quite as fast as proper RAM, so The Coalition essentially used the NVMe as a second tier of RAM to help the game's engine stream assets more smoothly. The game then swaps what's needed in the present moment to RAM, and then sends it back to the NVMe when it's not actively being used. "The benefit is that, in exchange for a couple of gigabytes of storage on the SSD, you can gain about a gigabyte of usable system memory," Digital Foundry's report explained. And, the system is smart enough to cherry-pick chunks of data that won't be heavily impacted by being moved to the slower memory. The system uses "advanced heuristics" to decide which data to move to the NVMe, by analysing access patterns. "Frequently used data stays in RAM, and anything idle can move to the SSD," the report added. Whether future Xbox games could use similar technology to increase performance on Xbox Series S is of course the big question, especially as large-world games GTA 6 and Fable approach. But though the execution may be unique to Gears of War: E-Day, the idea of swapping data between slow and fast memory isn't entirely new: Mac devices, for instance, are especially good at doing this. Yet as the current console generation ages, clever solutions will be needed to keep up with demands of triple-A games, especially as this generation may last longer than initially intended thanks to ongoing memory shortages . Incidentally, The Coalition also invested in other engine upgrades throughout E-Day development, such as improving the technology behind gore and dismemberment, because "we had this feeling fans were getting a bit desensitised to the violence in Gears" . It's a potentially important development for Xbox, but it comes at a time when Xbox is in no small amount of disarray as wide-ranging - and ongoing - restructuring rocks Microsoft's gaming division. Staff at The Coalition fear they could be laid off next, following the release of Gears of War: E-Day .

sources.title: Phoenix Cyclops joins MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls on November 2
sources.text: Details on the first Year 1 DLC character, PlayStation Plus Game Trial, and more. Hello everyone! I’m Takeshi Yamanaka, Producer of MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls . Today, we’re excited to reveal the gameplay trailer for Phoenix Cyclops, the first DLC character included in the Year 1 Pass for MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls. Arriving on November 2, Phoenix Cyclops (voiced by Ray Chase) brings a unique fighting style that combines a wide variety of Optic Blast attacks with the devastating power of the Phoenix Force. On the same day, Cyclops’ “Classic” and “Legacy” DLC costumes will also become available. If you’ve been waiting for Cyclops to join MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls and haven’t picked up the game yet, now is a great time to jump in. The game’s first-ever sale on PlayStation Store begins today, ahead of his arrival with the Ultimate Edition available at a discounted price. PlayStation Plus subscribers will also be able to try MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls with a 3-hour Game Trial starting today. Today, I’d like to share more about why we chose Phoenix Cyclops instead of the traditional version of Cyclops, the thought process behind his character design, his gameplay mechanics, and the inspiration behind his DLC costumes. Early in development, Cyclops was one of the leading candidates to join the roster as a member of the Unbreakable X-Men team. Cyclops has appeared in numerous Marvel fighting games over the years, and his visual identity and battle style have become firmly established through that long history. Because of that, we challenged ourselves to explore whether there was a way to present him in a style that felt different from what players had seen before. This became a major topic of discussion within the team. During those discussions, our narrative team proposed the idea of using the Phoenix version of Cyclops. We felt this interpretation would allow us to create fresher visuals and a more exciting fighting style while offering something unexpected for players. As a result, we made the difficult decision to continue working on the character until we felt like we were adding something new to his fighting game legacy. As a result, we’re excited to now release Phoenix Cyclops as our first post-launch DLC character. Phoenix Cyclops hopes to tame a destructive power to save mutantkind from extinction. This version of Scott Summers believes in absolute justice and is willing to make difficult decisions and take extreme actions when necessary. At the same time, we wanted to convey the inner conflict and emotional burden that comes with those choices. To help express that side of his personality, we intentionally gave him a somewhat younger appearance to contrast the incredible aura of the Phoenix Force. With Phoenix Cyclops’ transformed state, we wanted to illustrate his shift from idealistic leader to fiery corruption. While the overall Phoenix costume remains faithful to its source material, we incorporated details and visual touches inspired by the comics throughout the design process. Above all, our goal was simple: to make him look as cool as possible. Cyclops is designed as an all-rounder who excels at both long-range combat and close-range strikes through his versatile use of Optic Blasts. Empowered by the Phoenix Force, he can also unleash wide-area fire-based attacks that control large portions of the screen. In addition to projectiles, rushing attacks, throws, and setup tools, he has access to a wide variety of Optic Blast techniques. As players continue to use Optic Blasts, they accumulate Phoenix Force energy called Solar Shards. Once four Solar Shards have been collected, Cyclops can transform into his Dark Phoenix form. This mechanic was inspired by the Avengers vs. X-Men storyline, in which Cyclops became one of the Phoenix Five and eventually absorbed the power of his fellow teammates, transforming into Dark Phoenix. Entering Dark Phoenix form grants a significant temporary power boost, but it also comes with risks, including health depletion. The Phoenix Force is both an incredible source of power and a path to destruction. Successfully managing and controlling that power will be one of the keys to victory. When we decided to make Phoenix Cyclops the base version of the character, we understood that many fans would prefer the classic appearance they have known and loved for years. This isn’t unique to Cyclops. Anyone who grew up reading comics or watching animated adaptations has their own vision of what these characters should look like. Because of that, whenever we significantly reinterpret a character’s design or choose a relatively uncommon version of a character, we approach development with the expectation that classic-inspired costumes should also be available. The “Classic” and “Legacy” costumes were created with that philosophy in mind. We hope players enjoy experiencing Phoenix Cyclops in whichever style they prefer. It’s hard to believe that nearly two months have passed since launch. To everyone who continues to play the game every day, thank you for your incredible support. Players attending EVO France from October 9-11 will also have the opportunity to be among the first in the world to try Phoenix Cyclops. If you’re attending the event, we hope you’ll stop by the MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls booth and give him a try. Thank you again for your continued support, and we look forward to sharing more with you soon.

sources.text: Detalhes sobre o primeiro personagem de DLC do Ano 1, experimentação do jogo e mais. Oi, pessoal! Eu sou Takeshi Yamanaka, produtor de MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls . É uma alegria revelar o trailer de jogabilidade do Phoenix Cyclops, o primeiro personagem de DLC incluído no Passe do Ano 1 de MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls. Phoenix Cyclops, dublado por Ray Chase, chega em 2 de novembro com um estilo de luta único que combina uma grande variedade de ataques de explosão óptica com o poder devastador da Phoenix Force. Hoje, quero compartilhar mais sobre o motivo de termos escolhido o Phoenix Cyclops em vez da versão tradicional do Cyclops, as ideias por trás do design do personagem, as mecânicas de jogabilidade e a inspiração dos trajes de DLC. No início do desenvolvimento, o Cyclops era um dos principais candidatos para entrar na lista como membro da equipe Mutantes Indomáveis. Cyclops apareceu em vários jogos de luta da Marvel ao longo dos anos, e a identidade visual e o estilo de combate dele ficaram bem definidos nesse meio-tempo. Por isso, nós nos desafiamos a explorar a possibilidade de apresentá-lo com um estilo diferente e inédito para os jogadores. Esse se tornou um grande tópico de debate na equipe. Durante os debates, nossa equipe de narração sugeriu a ideia de usar a versão Phoenix do Cyclops. Acreditamos que esta interpretação nos permitiria criar um visual inovador e um estilo de luta mais empolgante, além de oferecer algo inesperado aos jogadores. Como resultado, tomamos a difícil decisão de remover o Cyclops da lista base e lançar o Phoenix Cyclops como o primeiro personagem de DLC pós-lançamento. Phoenix Cyclops tenta domar um poder destrutivo para salvar os mutantes da extinção. Esta versão do Scott Summers acredita na justiça absoluta e está disposta a tomar decisões difíceis e medidas extremas sempre que necessário. Ao mesmo tempo, queríamos transmitir o conflito interno e a carga emocional dessas escolhas. Para ajudar a expressar esse lado da personalidade dele, nós fizemos uma aparência mais jovem para contrastar com a aura incrível da Phoenix Force. Quanto ao estado transformado do Phoenix Cyclops, nós queríamos ilustrar a mudança de liderança sonhadora à corrupção feroz. Embora o traje geral de Phoenix continue fiel ao material original, nós incorporamos os detalhes e os toques visuais inspirados nos quadrinhos durante todo o processo de design. Acima de tudo, nosso objetivo era simples: deixá-lo o mais legal possível. Cyclops é um personagem versátil que se sai bem no combate de longo alcance e em golpes de curto alcance graças às explosões ópticas. Fortalecido pela Phoenix Force, ele também pode desferir ataques de fogo em área que controlam boa parte da tela. Além de projéteis, ataques de investida, arremessos e ferramentas de preparação, ele tem acesso a diversas técnicas de explosão óptica. Conforme os jogadores continuam usando as explosões ópticas, eles acumulam energia da Phoenix Force chamada de Fragmentos Solares. Depois de coletar quatro Fragmentos Solares, Cyclops pode se transformar em Phoenix Cyclops. Esta mecânica foi inspirada na história de Avengers vs. X-Men, em que Cyclops se tornou um dos Phoenix Five e acabou absorvendo o poder dos companheiros, transformando-se na Fênix Sombria. Entrar na forma de Fênix Sombria concede um grande aumento temporário de poder, mas também há riscos, como o esgotamento da saúde. A Phoenix Force é, ao mesmo tempo, uma fonte incrível de poder e o caminho para a destruição. Conseguir gerenciar e controlar esse poder será um dos segredos para a vitória. Quando decidimos que o Phoenix Cyclops seria a versão base do personagem, nós entendemos que muitos fãs prefeririam a aparência clássica que conhecem e adoram há anos. E isso não vale apenas para o Cyclops. Quem cresceu lendo os quadrinhos ou assistindo às adaptações animadas tem a própria visão em relação à aparência desses personagens. Por isso, sempre que fazemos uma grande reinterpretação do design ou escolhemos uma versão relativamente incomum de um personagem, encaramos o desenvolvimento com a expectativa de que trajes inspirados nos clássicos também devem ser disponibilizados. Os trajes “Clássico” e “Legado” foram criados com essa filosofia em mente. Esperamos que os jogadores se divirtam com o Phoenix Cyclops no estilo que quiserem. É difícil acreditar que quase dois meses se passaram desde o lançamento. Muito obrigado a todos que continuam jogando todos os dias. É um apoio incrível. Os jogadores que participarem do EVO França entre os dias 9 e 11 de outubro também terão a oportunidade de ser os primeiros do mundo a testar o Phoenix Cyclops. Se estiver participando do evento, esperamos que visitem o estande de MARVEL Tōkon: Fighting Souls e testem o personagem. Agradecemos de novo o apoio e estamos ansiosos para compartilhar mais novidades em breve.

sources.title: MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls DLC character Phoenix Cyclops launches November 2
sources.text: Four-versus-four tag fighting game MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls downloadable content character Phoenix Cyclops will launch on November 2, publisher Sony Interactive Entertainment and developer Arc System Works announced . Early in development, Cyclops was one of the leading candidates to join the roster as a member of the Unbreakable X-Men team. Cyclops has appeared in numerous Marvel fighting games over the years, and his visual identity and battle style have become firmly established through that long history. Because of that, we challenged ourselves to explore whether there was a way to present him in a style that felt different from what players had seen before. This became a major topic of discussion within the team. During those discussions, our narrative team proposed the idea of using the Phoenix version of Cyclops. We felt this interpretation would allow us to create fresher visuals and a more exciting fighting style while offering something unexpected for players. As a result, we made the difficult decision to continue working on the character until we felt like we were adding something new to his fighting game legacy. As a result, we’re excited to now release Phoenix Cyclops as our first post-launch DLC character. Phoenix Cyclops hopes to tame a destructive power to save mutantkind from extinction. This version of Scott Summers believes in absolute justice and is willing to make difficult decisions and take extreme actions when necessary. At the same time, we wanted to convey the inner conflict and emotional burden that comes with those choices. To help express that side of his personality, we intentionally gave him a somewhat younger appearance to contrast the incredible aura of the Phoenix Force. With Phoenix Cyclops’ transformed state, we wanted to illustrate his shift from idealistic leader to fiery corruption. While the overall Phoenix costume remains faithful to its source material, we incorporated details and visual touches inspired by the comics throughout the design process. Above all, our goal was simple: to make him look as cool as possible. Cyclops is designed as an all-rounder who excels at both long-range combat and close-range strikes through his versatile use of Optic Blasts. Empowered by the Phoenix Force, he can also unleash wide-area fire-based attacks that control large portions of the screen. In addition to projectiles, rushing attacks, throws, and setup tools, he has access to a wide variety of Optic Blast techniques. As players continue to use Optic Blasts, they accumulate Phoenix Force energy called Solar Shards. Once four Solar Shards have been collected, Cyclops can transform into his Dark Phoenix form. This mechanic was inspired by the Avengers vs. X-Men storyline, in which Cyclops became one of the Phoenix Five and eventually absorbed the power of his fellow teammates, transforming into Dark Phoenix. Entering Dark Phoenix form grants a significant temporary power boost, but it also comes with risks, including health depletion. The Phoenix Force is both an incredible source of power and a path to destruction. Successfully managing and controlling that power will be one of the keys to victory. When we decided to make Phoenix Cyclops the base version of the character, we understood that many fans would prefer the classic appearance they have known and loved for years. This isn’t unique to Cyclops. Anyone who grew up reading comics or watching animated adaptations has their own vision of what these characters should look like. Because of that, whenever we significantly reinterpret a character’s design or choose a relatively uncommon version of a character, we approach development with the expectation that classic-inspired costumes should also be available. The “Classic” and “Legacy” costumes were created with that philosophy in mind. We hope players enjoy experiencing Phoenix Cyclops in whichever style they prefer. It’s hard to believe that nearly two months have passed since launch. To everyone who continues to play the game every day, thank you for your incredible support. Players attending EVO France from October 9 to 11 will also have the opportunity to be among the first in the world to try Phoenix Cyclops. If you’re attending the event, we hope you’ll stop by the MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls booth and give him a try. MARVEL Tokon: Fighting Souls is available now for PlayStation 5 and PC via Steam and Epic Games Store .

stories.title: Resident Evil games engagement leapt 50% following release of Zach Cregger's movie, but analysts say real value is in brand building
stories.summary: Player engagement with Resident Evil games jumped 50% in the run up to and following the release of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, according to data shared exclusively with GamesIndustry.biz . Read more

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Resident Evil games engagement leapt 50% following release of Zach Cregger's movie, but analysts say real value is in brand building
sources.text: Resident Evil 2, which like the film is set in Raccoon City, saw a particularly high jump in daily active users Player engagement with Resident Evil games jumped 50% in the run up to and following the release of Zach Cregger's Resident Evil movie, according to data shared exclusively with GamesIndustry.biz . Sensor Tower looked at five Resident Evil titles across Steam, PlayStation, and Xbox, including Requiem, Resident Evil 2, Resident Evil 4, Village, and Biohazard. Daily active users (DAU) jumped 50% from 500,000 on August 30 to 750,000 on September 20. All five games saw increased engagement. Daily unit sales grew from 34,000 to nearly 80,000 over the same period. Looking at the overall Resident Evil franchise, Ampere Analysis found that DAU grew from 140,000 to 680,000 over the course of two weekends from September 6 to September 20. Cregger's film premiered on September 18. There were 540,000 players across the Resident Evil franchise on Sunday, September 6, which increased 11% to 600,000 the Sunday following. DAU increased a further 13% to 680,000 on the Sunday after the movie was released. Ampere's data covered 45 countries on PS, 32 countries on Xbox, and 41 countries on Steam. According to data from Newzoo, which was sourced from 37 markets excluding China, DAU across PC, PS, and Xbox averaged 72% higher than late-summer baselines five days following the film's release in most markets (September 16–18), reaching a peak of 282,526 on Sunday, September 20. Karl Kontus, SVP and general manager of Video Game Insights at Sensor Tower, notes that while these increases are significant, they start from a relatively low base "If we take a longer time frame view (last 12 months), these relative increases in DAU and unit sales from the movie's launch are very very small compared to the portfolio's overall performance," Kontus explains. "In fact, if you're looking at the cumulative units sold for Resident Evil Requiem, the movie launch's impact barely affects the game's overall performance." "The transmedia impact is clearly and measurably affecting game performance by increasing units sold and daily active users. We see this with Resident Evil as well as The Last of Us and Fallout," he continues. "However, this impact is typically very small in the context of the overall game's performance – a single-digit percentage uplift to units and revenue. Ampere Analysis' Piers Harding-Rolls agrees: "The Resident Evil movie has had a sizable positive impact on activity and sales of Resident Evil games across consoles and PC. However, while growth has been noteworthy, the actual volumes involved are small. With an estimated 6 million+ tickets for the movie being sold, the impact has been relatively minor in that context." "The benefit of these transmedia initiatives isn't the short-term increase in game sales. It's IP and brand building. Staying relevant in the players' and watchers' minds. It guarantees that future game launches will remain successful." Discounts also heavily influenced engagement metrics. Capcom cut prices across the series from September 8 on Steam and September 10 on consoles, which lifted DAUs by 21% prior to the film's release. Harding-Rolls also highlights that there was a 30% discount on Requiem across platforms from September 7 to coincide with the film launch. However, "in volume terms the impact on sales [on Requiem] has been relatively lightweight." "This recent discount follows another reduction that took place in late May and early June, which is likely to have reduced the impact during this second discounting campaign." Newzoo's data found that engagement across the Resident Evil franchise rose "sharply" during the film's opening weekend, driven primarily by Resident Evil 2. Emmanuel Rosier, director of marketing intelligence at Newzoo, says Resident Evil 2 attracted players because it "was the cheapest way in" to the franchise at $7.99, a sixth of the discounted price. "The pattern suggests the film sends players to the entry point that matches what they just watched, rather than to the newest game." Rosier adds that Resident Evil 2 saw the most activity because the film shares its setting. "The film's director, Zach Cregger, has described the film as a story running in parallel to Raccoon City's outbreak, the setting of Resident Evil 2, and that is where the game players went back to. Its DAU came close to five times baseline after release, up from under twice baseline during the price cut, and rose on all three platforms at once." That's in contrast to Sensor Tower's data, which demonstrated that Resident Evil 4 and Requiem had much more of an effect on engagement than Resident Evil 2. Rosier noted that Resident Evil 2's engagement rate closely followed the DAU pattern of Assassin's Creed Odyssey in July , with one key difference. "Christopher Nolan's Odyssey opened on July 17, and a PlayStation-only discount followed on July 25," said Rosier. "This time, the discounts came first, on Steam from September 8 and on PlayStation and Xbox from September 10, and the film followed eight to 10 days later. The 38% jump from September 18 to 19 came on top of prices that were already cut." Reviewing engagement increases for both Odyssey and Resident Evil 2, Rosier notes that "the game closest to the film moves most," which then lifts the broader franchise. "Odyssey, set in ancient Greece, rose far more than the rest of the Assassin's Creed catalogue. Resident Evil 2, set during the Raccoon City outbreak that Cregger's story runs in parallel to, rose to nearly five times its baseline, well ahead of Requiem, the newest release. Other Assassin's Creed titles rose about 1.4 times from the film's opening, while the Resident Evil franchise total rose 72% after release."

sources.title: Warhammer Survivors launches November 10, new characters revealed
sources.text: A glimpse at two newly announced characters and their devastating weapons. Today, we’re excited to announce that Warhammer Survivors launches on PS5 November 10 . To mark the occasion we’re also revealing two characters in our latest trailer. Eagle-eyed fans who have been following the game for a while may have noticed Morvenn Vahl in the game’s key art, and we’re really excited to show her off in full pixel art glory finally. Warhammer Survivors allows you to play in both the Warhammer 40,000 and Warhammer Age of Sigmar universe, so her counterpart (as part of today’s reveal) is Lyssa Revenya, a skilled thief and tomb-robber. While both champions take prime position in today’s spotlight, they couldn’t be more different. Formerly a young Celestian Superior, Morvenn Vahl was chosen to become High Abbess Sanctorum – supreme commander of Adepta Sororitas. Vahl is an iron-willed warrior, suffering no fools and certainly no heretics. Dissatisfied with commanding from the safety of the Imperium, Vahl spearheads many crusades personally, leading from the front. As one of our larger Warhammer Survivors characters, Vahl strides across the battlefield in her ornate Paragon Warsuit. She’s armed with the devastating Heavy Bolter Fidelis, which sprays an arc of projectiles obliterating her foes. The weapon also has a chance to trigger a miracle, blessing Vahl and increasing the weapon’s rate of fire. Fidelis can be evolved to the Purgator Mirabilis, which unlocks the use of the warsuit’s Paragon Missile Launcher, unleashing a sporadic salvo of explosions across the battlefield – in addition to Fidelis’ spray of bolter shells. Lyssa Revenya is a talented thief and an integral member of the Saviours of Cinderfall, a rag-tag band of heroes who scoured the streets of Hammerhal and put an end to those plotting the city’s demise. Originally hailing from Lethis, Lyssa is well-versed in the art of navigating trap-ridden crypts and catacombs of that morbid city. In Warhammer Survivors, Lyssa turns her signature tools for breaking and entering into weapons. The Rope and Grapnel shoot hooks in from random edges of the screen, colliding with specific points on the battlefield, damaging enemies and dragging away any who survive. It’s the perfect weapon for a nimble thief who likes to stay more than a sword-length from their enemies. When the Rope and Grapnel evolves, Lyssa communes with the spirit of Rhea, a former ally and mentor. This terrifying, screaming banshee soars across the battlefield, exploding into a vengeful cloud of damaging ghostly fog. Perhaps in the right hands, Lyssa’s Rope and Grapnel can be utilised to pull enemies toward the Ghost of Rhea’s vengeful uproars? There’s only one way to find out. Warhammer Survivors launches on November 10; Morvenn Vahl and Lyssa Revenya are just two of over 40 playable champions waiting for you in-game. You can wishlist and pre-order on PlayStation 5 starting today, and PlayStation Plus members will receive a 10% discount when pre-ordering.

sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day – Surviving the First Night of Emergence
sources.text: Today marks the worldwide launch of Gears of War: E-Day , now available on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, Game Pass and Steam. One of XBOX’s most iconic sagas returns to where it all began, taking players back to the opening hours of Emergence Day and the catastrophic event that changed the world of Sera forever. Emergence Day is a defining moment for the Gears of War universe – the catastrophic event changed the world of Sera forever, but the story of that fateful night has never been fully told, until now. Gears of War: E-Day transports us back to the opening hours of the Locust invasion, where an unsuspecting world is ruthlessly plunged into chaos as monsters erupt from underground. Across three harrowing days and nights, Marcus Fenix, Dom Santiago and their fierce new squad mates fight desperately to survive the onslaught consuming the city of Kalona, while uncovering the true scale of a threat unlike anything they – or humanity – has ever faced. From the moment the prologue opens, Gears of War: E-Day showcases a masterclass in action-horror. This is not the Locust enemy you’ve fought before. They’re equally cunning as they are violent, and frankly, you should be terrified to face them. If this is your first deployment, or you’re coming out of retirement to fight the war ahead, we’ve got you covered. Before you step out onto the streets of Kalona, here are a few things every Gear should know. Gears of War is famously a cover-based shooter, and you’ll rely on it to stay alive as you push through the Locust. Keep your head down and dip from cover-to-cover – and avoid walking out into the open unless you’re rushing an enemy with a melee attack. Even a handful of Drones can deal massive damage while you’re exposed, which can be trouble for both you and the squadmate that may have to come and revive you. Sometimes, the best course of action is to hold patiently and pick off enemies as they come, and there’s no shame in that strategy. Sometimes, you’ll just need to haul ass and stay as mobile as you can, which I quickly learned during an early fight with a Brumak wielding a horrible chain weapon. There’s no peace to be found in cover for that situation – fan out, keep it distracted, and pray that it doesn’t decide to charge you while your gun is jammed. Each weapon you’ll find in E-Day is deeply situational, which makes for a great tactical experience. The Chainsaw Lancer is a great all-rounder, offering close-to-mid range firepower and a big ol’ (upgradeable) mag to chew through. The Gnasher is a stellar shotgun, fantastic for devastating point-blank damage. The Longshot Sniper, one of my personal favorites, pops a slick, long-range slug into unsuspecting foes from a great distance. Not only is that incredibly satisfying each time, but it lets you get a stack of damage into a tankier enemy – like a Boomer, before it gets close to you. There are caches dotted around Kalona that let you switch up your loadout, too, so don’t feel like you’re locked into a specific style of play forever. Mix up your strategy, swap roles with your friends, but above all – experiment! I know I said this is a cover-based shooter, but sometimes you’ll need to resort to more personal measures. Before E-Day even lets you look at a gun, it hands out a crash course in melee – one of the most useful, life-saving abilities for a Gear. Spend some time getting to grips with how it works when wielding a metal pipe and the Snub pistol – figure out the weight of the swing, and how it feels to hit enemies in front, and more importantly, behind you. Later, melee becomes even more fun with the Chainsaw Lancer, and you’ll feel extra confident with it once you’ve got the basics of backhanding down. As soon as you pop your head up to aim a shot, you’re a giant bullet magnet, effectively inviting every weapon-wielder on the map to pop you like a balloon. Fortunately, Gears can shoot blind from behind cover, which is a superb way to dish out additional damage to something getting too close for comfort. If you don’t have the health to rush out for a melee takedown, or you need a few seconds of recovery time, blind fire from cover is a clutch move to get the job done. While E-Day ‘s campaign is primarily linear, Kalona has large pockets of open space with multiple pathways towards the next objective, as well as side paths that may lead to side missions. These are smaller, optional objectives that let you support other squads, help civilians, and otherwise contribute to saving the city. Not only do they offer additional insight into the wider story, you’ll also get a nice reward for doing it, often a weapon mod. While you’re exploring, keep an ear open for a sharp chime whenever you enter a new area of the city – anywhere from inside a building to a side street. That means there’s a collectable nearby. These range from familiar items like COG armor and tags, to esoteric pieces like… a can of soup. They all come with great little lore entries too, some written by the squad members themselves. It’s a wonderful added insight into their stories, and the wider world, so pick them up when you can. Now that you’re equipped with the basics, there’s only one thing left to do – get out there. Gather your squad, load up, and uncover the world-shattering event that started it all. Gears of War: E-Day is available today on XBOX Series X|S, XBOX on PC, Game Pass and Steam. Play it on both console and PC at no additional cost with XBOX Play Anywhere.

sources.title: Gears of War E-Day Is a 'Natural Choice to Be an Exclusive' – Studio Head Mike Crump Claims Series Carries the Banner for Xbox
sources.text: Gears of War: E-Day launched this week, and while it is excellent, the game was pulled away from a PS5 launch earlier this year. In a recent interview, The Coalition Studio Head Mike Crump claims that this was all part of the plan. In an interview with the BBC , Crump defended the choice to be an Xbox exclusive, despite a likely ludicrous budget saying, "Gears has been an exclusive franchise to Xbox for 20 years now. It's sort of entwined deeply with the brand." However, Gears of War: Reloaded did launch on PS5 last year, so the franchise as a whole isn't exactly Xbox-exclusive anymore. It's also likely that if E-Day did launch on PlayStation, it'd see higher sales numbers. Crump claims that the metrics for success go further than that, though. He told the BBC that the series is meant to, at least in part, carry the banner for the Xbox platform and give people a "reason to be in the Xbox ecosystem." Queue Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's decision to pull the game from the PS5 release slate. Regardless, the game will now likely have lower sales than it otherwise would have. When the BBC asked Crump about that, he insisted that the studio is taking a broader view than just looking at sales figures and retention numbers. "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to it limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? ...Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware," he answered. If the goal is to be a tech demo about what the Xbox consoles are capable of, I'd argue that it's a straight-up success. The game looks incredible on both the Xbox Series X and Series S, so much so that The Coalition had to rely on trickery with the Page File to get the game running smoothly on the less-powerful console. The game is also incredible, and our reviewer Ryan McCaffrey gave it a 9 , saying: "By going back to the beginning, Gears of War: E-Day returns to the heart of this series: Marcus Fenix, Dom Santiago, and a Locust horde that’s as terrifying as it is dangerous. E-Day pulls off the tightrope act of giving us a heartfelt prequel with strong characters even when we know how it ends. On a more mechanical level, it also evolves the enemies, weapons, and combat you’d expect to deliver a Gears of War campaign that stands toe-to-toe with any of the others. It wraps up with 10 years still left to go before Marcus gets tossed in prison ahead of the events of the first Gears of War, so here’s hoping the next one stays in the past for a while longer – and that we don’t have to wait another seven years for it to arrive." But even if the game is a critical hit and a technical marvel, sales numbers will inevitably play a role in the game's success, especially as Microsoft is currently in the middle of a months-long restructuring campaign. Right after launch, developers at The Coalition told Eurogamer they were expecting layoffs. However, Crump has since addressed those concerns , saying, "For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that." Let's just hope that a pretty game and high review scores really are enough to keep the Xbox layoff machine at bay. Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

Netflix just announced The Conjuring: Unspoken , a new horror game set in The Conjuring universe that you can play with your phone as a controller, and it will launch exclusively on the service on October 13th. According to sources familiar with Microsoft’s plans, Sharma’s brief teaser was actually about Xbox managing to land a deal for game streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto VI . The deal will mean Xbox Cloud Gaming can stream Grand Theft Auto VI to players at launch, but it’s not clear how long the agreement will be in place. Rockstar Games still hasn’t announced a PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI , and a streaming deal would normally also allow Xbox to market its Xbox Cloud Gaming service to PC players who would otherwise need an Xbox Series X / S or PS5 console. After The Verge originally reported that the deal would be exclusive, Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball revealed on X that Microsoft wouldn’t be streaming Grand Theft Auto VI exclusively, nor to PCs. That suggests the deal is simply for Xbox console streaming, and may mean the web browsers and apps that can usually access Xbox Cloud Gaming will not be able to stream Grand Theft Auto VI . News of the streaming rights comes around a month after Microsoft announced some major changes to Xbox Cloud Gaming . From November, the same month Grand Theft Auto VI releases, Microsoft is limiting streaming hours to just 15 hours for Xbox Game Pass Ultimate subscribers, 10 hours for Premium subscribers, and just five hours for Game Pass Essential. Microsoft is also opening up access to Xbox Cloud Gaming with a pay-as-you-go option next month, rather than being limited to Game Pass subscriptions. The pay-as-you-go option is perfectly timed for Grand Theft Auto VI , allowing those who don’t own an Xbox, or who primarily play from a phone, to stream the game by paying for a bundle of hours. During the Xbox all-hands, Sharma also told employees that Project Helix, the next generation of Xbox hardware, will be a “family of devices” and that Microsoft will partner with others on some of those devices. Sharma first called Helix a family of devices last month in an interview, after Microsoft and AMD announced a “ strategic multi-year partnership ” last year to work together on “a portfolio of devices,” including Microsoft’s next-generation Xbox console. Correction, October 6th : Xbox has clarified that its streaming deal isn’t exclusive and Grand Theft Auto VI won’t be streamed to PCs.

sources.text: Excitement "has led to some misreporting". Xbox has denied reports suggesting it obtained exclusive game-streaming rights for Grand Theft Auto 6 . The initial suggestion came from a report on The Verge , which cited an all-hands meeting in which CEO Asha Sharma allegedly told staff that Xbox plans to do something "no other platform holder is doing" around GTA 6. The report inferred that Xbox had acquired exclusive game streaming rights for GTA 6, which would allow anyone using Xbox's Cloud Gaming service to stream GTA 6 on any supported platform - including on PC where the game won't natively be available. Shortly after the report was published, however, Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball took to X to quash the suggestion and said Xbox won't be streaming GTA 6 exclusively , nor will the game be available that way on PC. "While the excitement for GTA 6 and Xbox is great to see," Ball said, "it has also led to some misreporting. If it is, an Xbox user would need to purchase a copy of GTA 6 and subscribe to Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream the game to - seemingly - anything but a PC. Following Sharma's appointment as CEO, the company has capped the number of Cloud Gaming play-hours available to Game Pass members . After years of no limits, Game Pass users are now limited to just 15 hours per month at the highest tier, Ultimate, which is reportedly a tipping-point where the streaming service stops being profitable for Microsoft . In November, perhaps timed around the launch of GTA 6, Xbox is also launching Xbox Cloud Gaming as a standalone service that anyone can use without the need for a Game Pass membership. This paid model allows users to buy chunks of playtime hours to stream games they own to supported devices. Xbox is also exploring different business models around game streaming. The company is already testing an ad-supported, free tier of Cloud Gaming with Xbox Insiders , and a November launch for that tier would make sense. Beyond the Xbox portion of the report, Rockstar has not announced any GTA 6 streaming deals with any provider, though that could change as we get closer to the game's 19th November release date.

sources.title: Unity unveils a web-based AI game creation platform
sources.text: Unity Spark will launch later this year on Google Playground Today marks the launch of Playground, a new Google platform for generating games using natural language prompts, and it will soon host a version of Unity based around generative AI agents. Unity Spark , which runs on the Unity engine, will be launching in beta later this year. The tool will allow users to design and iterate on 3D games via text prompts, and it is entirely browser-based, with no download required. Both Unity Spark and Playground will only be available to users aged 18+. Although announced as a strategic partnership with Google, Unity Spark will use a variety of generative AI models, and is not exclusively tied to Google's AI technology. Unity Spark is linked to the Unity Asset Store; in a demo given to GamesIndustry.biz , a text prompt asking for a cape for the main character brought up a range of suggested items from the store. Another prompt asked for a sunrise background, and the AI agent provided a range of options. The agent can also make suggestions based on the user's actions, such as offering to create a tool for toggling between different lighting presets, and multiple agents can be set to work at the same time. In a blog post , Unity CEO Matt Bromberg said that Unity Spark wasn't about "one-shotting" – that is, generating an entire game from a single prompt – and is instead about building something "worth working on, polishing, and sharing." "It's about using the new technology to enable more people to express themselves," he said. "And it all begins with the game art. Unity Spark connects directly to the Unity Asset Store, so you can build with thousands of high-quality, artist-created assets made by our community. "We made Unity Spark for the gamers who have spent a thousand hours inside a genre and know exactly what's missing. The graphic artist who wants to bring their vision to life but doesn't know how to code. Modders who now want to create something entirely new. That's the opportunity we see: Folks with real creative conviction who can now fulfill their full potential." Multiple users can work on the same project at the same time by sharing a link, and projects can be published on Google Playground. The Unity Spark editor only runs on desktop browsers, but games made with the system can be played on both desktop and mobile browsers. At launch, it won't be possible to download projects or export them to the full desktop version of the Unity engine. It also won't be possible to sell any projects created with Unity Spark at launch. Payment for Unity Spark will involve a credit-based system, which is tied to AI tokens. Access to a certain amount of credits will be free, after which users will have to buy credits, although the full details of the payment system haven't been finalised. But rather than being designed to generate a profit, Unity's main aim for the system is to encourage more people to make games. "Producing a polished experience of your own has long been beyond the capabilities of most people," said Bromberg. "As a consequence, although about 3 billion people play a game made with Unity each month, almost none of them have ever made one. Electronic games are the last major form of entertainment that nearly everyone consumes but almost nobody creates. That's something we'd like to help change. "We don't know exactly who will walk through this door, or what they'll make. That's the whole point. Democratizing game creation is Unity's founding mission. Unity Spark was incubated in that spirit. We can't wait to see what you build together." Unity has been steadily building a suite of generative AI tools for its game engine. A number of them were launched in open beta in May , including a 'Plan' mode for designing implementation steps and 'Skills' for guidance in areas like UI creation. In August, Bromberg credited the company's growth in revenue to the ongoing success of Unity Vector AI . The upcoming Unity 7, which launches in Q1 2027, will feature AI tools as a core component, although Unity's senior vice president of product Adam Smith has emphasised that developers are not required to use them . "If your studio has committed to keeping AI out of your creative work – you're not on the sidelines of this release," he said.

sources.title: Undead Labs speaks about its split from Xbox, revealing it has to "make some changes" to State of Decay 3 following layoffs
sources.text: Parting with colleagues was "total heartbreak". State of Decay studio Undead Labs has spoken out after rebuying its independence and leaving Xbox last month, revealing it has "got to make some changes" to State of Decay 3 because of layoffs it suffered as a result. Studio boss Phillip Holt said this during a wide-ranging conversation with The Game Business , in which he detailed the studio's shifting priorities now it has no "boss" to respond to other than its audience, and while explaining why the co-op zombie survival game seems to have been in development for ages. "We're pretty close to finishing this game," Holt said. "And there's a lot in it. I think folks that saw us at Gamescom can attest to that. I think our alpha players can attest to that. And obviously, with a significant number of people leaving the company, we've got to make some changes. But I don't think we're dramatically addressing scope in that way." State of Decay 3 currently has a vague release date of "2027" , announced this summer, which allows Undead Labs some scheduling wiggle-room. But the game was originally revealed all the way back in 2020 , before slipping out of view for a long time, leading people to wonder about what was going on. "I don't think it's taken that long, actually," Holt remarked, when speaking about the game's long development. "If you measure it from when State of Decay 2 shipped, yeah, we're approaching eight years. If you measure it from our first trailer with the infamous zombie deer, that's also a long time. I got myself in a little bit of trouble by saying we didn't really have a team working on the game at that point, which wasn't entirely true, we had a very small team. We've had a small team on the game since maybe 2020. But development didn't really pick up until 2022 or 2023." But why did Undead Labs announce the third State of Decay game so early? The answer is eerily prophetic, and it's to do with the spending spree Microsoft was on when it acquired Undead Labs in 2018 - the same spending spree that saw it acquire Ninja Theory, Compulsion Games, and Playground Games (two of which are also no longer a part of Xbox). Holt wanted to announce State of Decay 3 before Undead Labs was "swallowed up or divested" by the rest of a much bigger gaming division, he said. "I didn't think Microsoft was done being acquisitive," Holt explained, "and I didn't think they'd continue buying small developers - I assumed they'd start buying big things. I was a little worried about getting swallowed up or divested before we had a chance to present to the world what we were working on. So, it was a bit of a marker on the table. I was saying, 'State of Decay 3, we're announcing it, the audience knows it's in development, and here's a trailer to demonstrate our vision.'" Undead Labs was eventually earmarked for divestiture this summer when Xbox announced its major restructuring . At the time, Undead Labs was said to have "entered terms to join new ownership", but that new-ownership deal - as in the case of Ninja Theory - never actually materialised. "We had a lot of interest," Holt assured The Game Business, but when he heard other studios were doing management buyouts, he submitted one for Undead Labs, "and Microsoft thought that would be a good idea". Holt wouldn't say how many people were laid off as a result of the studio downsizing to operate independently, "because these are our friends and colleagues and it was a total heartbreak to have to part ways". "I would hate to reduce the impact to those individuals to a number or statistic," he said. But he insisted the studio had "everything we need to ship State of Decay 3", and that its mission was now even clearer. "Inside of a larger company, you serve multiple objectives and you have directives that you need to achieve," Holt said. "Now it's just: make the best possible game. Of course, inside Xbox, that was also the primary objective. But it's just a cleaner, clearer line of sight to the audience. I don't have a boss. The success or failure of the company is down to whether we create something an audience will support.” State of Decay 3 will still launch on Game Pass on day one, and Holt praised Xbox's subscription service as being partly responsible for the series' ongoing success, which has apparently seen it reach 25 million players over its lifetime. "I don't know that we'd be in the place we are today if not for the Game Pass audience," he acknowledged. "Even today, we have several thousand people coming through the door every day." Dom had a chance to play State of Decay 3 and echoed what Holt said above, that the game was looking good. They're hoping to find some time to write more fully about it soon. (Ask them about it in the comments!)

sources.title: Google now lets you make games with AI
sources.text: Google Playground is a browser-based tool for making games from AI prompts. Google Playground is a browser-based tool for making games from AI prompts. Google today announced Playground, a new browser-based platform for making custom games from AI prompts. Playground will be available today in the US for users who are 18 and older at playground.google. The company is pitching it as an “experimental gaming platform” that “lowers the barriers to creation” and doesn’t require coding experience. “With Playground’s conversational interface, you can direct the game just by typing what you want to build,” Google says in a blog post . “Start from a blank canvas, remix starter prompts, or use guided support to shape your concept — and then test it right away. Want to tweak the physics, rewrite the rules, customize the characters, or overhaul the environment? Just ask. You stay in complete control of the creative direction from rough concept to final polish.” When you’re finished making your game, you can share it with a link or publish it to the “Playground Explore gallery” so others can play it. “Select genres” will support in-game leaderboards and multiplayer. The gallery will highlight games that are “fresh, creative, and fun” using ratings and play activity, according to Google. Playground is free to use, but if you have a Google One subscription, you’ll have higher weekly token limits based on your plan, Google spokesperson Nia Carter tells The Verge . Under the hood, Playground is powered by “Google’s existing foundation models (Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria) paired with a custom harness refined through our own internally built games and evaluations,” Carter says. Alongside today’s Playground announcement, Google and Unity are also revealing Unity Spark , an AI game-making experience that’s closer to a professional-level game development engine and allows you to create games simultaneously with others. Games made with Unity Spark will be shareable on Playground. A closed beta for Spark is scheduled to kick off later this year, and people who are interested can get on a waitlist starting today. Google’s news today follows Meta’s recent announcement that it will let users build games with AI on their phones and on the web for its Horizon platform with new apps rolling out in early access. Published games made with those tools will be able to be recommended on Facebook and Instagram, which could give them more reach than they would have just being on Horizon. Roblox has also started letting users make games with AI on their phones as part of a “Build” feature that’s in public alpha testing in a few countries.

sources.text: Bit Reactor CEO Greg Foertsch calls it an "important step forward" Star Wars: Zero Company maker Bit Reactor is bringing back developers who were furloughed ahead of launch. "This week, we started the process of returning more of our team back to work at Bit Reactor, an important step forward in our continued support for Zero Company," studio CEO Greg Foertsch said in an online statement from today.
